newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice allows ADM deal with Mexico's Gruma.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice allows ADM deal with Mexico's Gruma.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department said Friday it approved a $280 million deal between Archer-Daniels-Midland Co and Mexico's Gruma SA de CV after the two tortilla flour makers agreed to divest a flour mill in Texas.

As a result of the restructuring, ADM will be allowed to acquire 22 pct of Gruma stock and will have to sell its flour mill in Muleshoe, Texas, the department said, adding that the two companies will be able to form a partnership to combine their U.S. flour milling operations.
The Justice Department said the state of Texas also agreed to the deal involving the two largest U.S. tortilla flour manufacturers.
It said approval of the deal is conditioned on the sale of ADM's flour mill in Texas to Minsa SA de CV, a Mexican firm which also has a mill in Iowa.

"Without this settlement, consumers would pay more for tortillas, chips and other products because a single dominant firm would have been able to raise prices of masa flour, an essential ingredient," Acting Assistant Attorney general Joel Klein said in a statement.
More than a billion pounds of the milled corn flour are produced each year in the United States, with a wholesale value between $200 and $300 million, the department estimated.
